subject: Changing Fixed Effects values when Predicting

messages.author: 122025c7cfb67f4e
messages.subject: Changing Fixed Effects values when Predicting
parts:
Hello, 
Apologies if there's a very simple answer to this question, but I'm pretty new to working with INLA. I am currently working on a distribution model for a wildlife species based on habitat and climatic conditions, and was familiarizing myself with the methods for spatial predictions in INLA. I noticed that the values of the fixed effects for my model are different when the data contains just the data used to fit the model (estimation values) versus when it contains a joined stack of estimated and prediction values (in my case a grid of spatial locations with response=NA). I've included some example code below. The differences in values for the fixed effects and other model outputs in the example data between Swiss.output (est & pred stacks) & Swiss.output.est (just est stack) are small (they're larger in my own project unfortunately, one of the coefficient values change from 9.3 to 8.7), but shouldn't they be identical regardless? 
I guess I don't quite understand why the values would change if the prediction stack is included since I'm not estimating the parameter values from the prediction data, or perhaps I'm doing something or interpreting something wrong. 
Any insight would be greatly appreciated. 
Cheers,
Evan

library(geoR)
sic.all
sic.all$coords[,1]<-(sic.all$coords[,1]-apply(sic.borders,2,mean)[1])
sic.all$coords[,2]<-(sic.all$coords[,2]-apply(sic.borders,2,mean)[2])
sic.borders<-apply(sic.borders,2,scale,scale=F)

index.est<-which(as.numeric(rownames(sic.all$coords))
                 %in% as.numeric(rownames(sic.100$coords)))

est.coord<-sic.all$coords[index.est,]
est.data<-sqrt(sic.all$data[index.est])
est.elevation<-sic.all$covariate$altitude[index.est]/1000

val.coord<-sic.all$coords[-index.est,]
val.data<-sqrt(sic.all$data[-index.est])
val.elevation<-(sic.all$covariate$altitude[-index.est])/1000

library(gstat)
data(sic97)

x.res<-demstd@gri...@cells.dim[1]
y.res<-demstd@gri...@cells.dim[2]

pred.elevation<-as.matrix(demstd@data)
elevation.grid<-matrix(pred.elevation,nrow=x.res,ncol=y.res,byrow = F)
elevation.grid<-elevation.grid[,y.res:1]/1000
dim(elevation.grid)

seq.x.grid<-seq(from=demstd@coords[1,1], to=demstd@coords[2,1],
                length=x.res/1000)
seq.y.grid<-seq(from=demstd@coords[1,2], to=demstd@coords[2,2],
                length=y.res)/1000
pred.grid<-as.matrix(expand.grid(x=seq.x.grid,y=seq.y.grid))

Swiss.mesh<-inla.mesh.2d(loc.domain=sic.borders, max.edge=c(35,100))
plot(Swiss.mesh)
Swiss.spde<-inla.spde2.matern(mesh=Swiss.mesh, alpha=2)
A.est<-inla.spde.make.A(mesh=Swiss.mesh, loc=est.coord)
A.val<-inla.spde.make.A(mesh=Swiss.mesh,loc=val.coord)

s.index<-inla.spde.make.index(name="spatial.field", n.spde=Swiss.spde$n.spde)

stack.est<-inla.stack(data=list(rain=est.data),
                      A=list(A.est,1),
                      effects=list(c(s.index,list(Intercept=1)),
                                   list(Elevation=est.elevation)),
                      tag="est")
stack.val<-inla.stack(data=list(rain=NA),
                      A=list(A.val,1),
                      effects=list(c(s.index,list(Intercept=1)),
                                   list(Elevation=val.elevation)),
                      tag="val")
join.stack<-inla.stack(stack.est, stack.val)

formula<-rain~-1+Intercept+Elevation+f(spatial.field,model=spde)

Swiss.output<-inla(formula,
                   data=inla.stack.data(join.stack, spde=Swiss.spde),
                   family="gaussian",
                   control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(join.stack), compute=TRUE),
                   control.compute=list(cpo=TRUE, dic=TRUE))
summary(Swiss.output)


Swiss.output.est<-inla(formula,
                   data=inla.stack.data(stack.est, spde=Swiss.spde),
                   family="gaussian",
                   control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack.est), compute=TRUE),
                   control.compute=list(cpo=TRUE, dic=TRUE))
summary(Swiss.output.est)


Cheers,
Evan
